title: Give employees long service leave
what: Give each employee long service leave (or payment in lieu) once they reach the qualifying period of service, and keep long service leave records.

sources.title: Long Service Leave Act 1955 (NSW)
sources.publisher: NSW Legislation (via the Open Australian Legal Corpus)
sources.quote: (1) Except as otherwise provided in this Act, every worker shall be entitled to long service leave on ordinary pay in respect of the service of the worker with an employer.

sources.title: Long Service Leave Act 1955 (NSW)
sources.publisher: NSW Legislation (via the Open Australian Legal Corpus)
sources.quote: (1) An employer must ensure a long service leave record is kept in relation to each worker employed by the employer.

sources.title: Long Service Leave Act 1955 (NSW)

sources.quote: Inspector means an inspector appointed under the Industrial Relations Act 1996.

reach.note: Every employer of workers in NSW, except where the Act's exemptions apply (for example, an approved scheme).

confidence_note: Quoted from the Open Australian Legal Corpus copy of the version shown (DECISIONS E-118); later changes not checked.

assessment.summary: Employers must give long service leave after a long period of service with them. The entitlement builds up with one employer and is mostly lost on moving, which ties workers to employers; it also adds record keeping.

marks.reason: Leave builds up with one employer and is mostly lost on moving, which discourages job changes (unlike portable schemes).

assessment.confidence_note: Marked from the law's design against the framework's guide; no evaluation of state long service leave and job mobility was found.
